editorial:
Imagine being a talented director who has lost everything. That is exactly where you find Victor. He is dealing with a lot of pain after his wife passed away, and he has fallen into a dark hole of drinking and unemployment. But despite the sadness, he has a special bond with his nine-year-old son, Ingmar. To keep the kid's spirits up, Victor tells him wild, imaginative stories based on movie scripts he wants to film one day. It is a bittersweet vibe where the grey reality of their poor living conditions clashes with the bright, colorful worlds of robots and sci-fi that they build together in their minds.

You will really feel for the chemistry between the father and son; it is the strongest part of the whole movie. The acting feels real and raw, though the pacing is a bit slow in the middle. While it gets heavy when people start doubting if Victor is fit to be a dad, the heart of the story keeps you invested. If you are in the mood for a tear-jerker, you should definitely check this out. Try streaming it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video for the best picture, or just rent it on Apple TV for a cozy night in.
endingExplained: The movie ends with a focus on healing and the bond between father and son. After facing the threat of losing Ingmar, Victor realizes he cannot hide in his fantasies or his bottle anymore. He decides to finally face his grief and get his life together for his son. The final scenes show a glimmer of hope, suggesting that while the pain of loss stays, their love and shared imagination will help them move forward together.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves stories about family bonds and overcoming grief.
